paper.title: Distributionally Robust Policy Gradient for Offline Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Offline contextual bandits (off-policy optimization from logged data)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline policy learning from a pre-collected logged dataset (no interaction); guarantees are policy-gradient estimation error and convergence to a stationary point, not regret.
unmapped: offline dataset generated by a known logging policy beta
parameterized policy pi_theta optimized by policy gradient
objective is stationarity of the value function (gradient norm)
the learner knows the logging policy beta
settings.definition_quote: In this paper, we study the problem of offline policy optimization, where during the learning process we only have access to an offline dataset Dlog = {(xi, ai, r(xi, ai))} generated by a specific logging policy β(a|x), x ∈ X, a ∈ A. In other words, we are not allowed to interact with the environment.

symbols.Rad_S: empirical Rademacher complexity of F on S

conditions: logging dataset i.i.d. from logging policy beta
reward class F with sup |r - r'| <= M

source.quote: With probability at least 1 − δ, the generalization bound of policy gradient estimation satisfies: Eπθt [∥ĝ(θt) − ∇V πθt ∥22] ≤ G2 W [(2RB + σ0−2)−1 + λ + 4M ℜ̂S(F) + 3M2 √(1/(2|S|) log(2/δ))].

results.notes: Bound on mean-squared error of the policy gradient estimate, not regret. Main-text extraction appears to show W^2, while Lemma A.1/Theorem A.2 show W; used W. Builds on Theorem 1 of Liu et al. (2020).

source.quote: Under the same conditions as Theorem 4.4, assume that the value function V πθ is always L-smooth for every θ, and that we run at least T iterations for policy gradient learning with step size η = 1/(4L). Then the output πθT̂ of Algorithm 1 satisfies: E[∥∇V πθT̂ ∥22] ≤ 4/(T η)(V πθT+1 − V πθ1) + 3G2 W [(2RB + σ0−2)−1 + λ + 4M ℜ̂S(F) + 3M2 √(1/(2|S|) log(2/δ))].

results.notes: Stationarity guarantee (expected squared gradient norm), not regret; T is number of policy gradient iterations. The statistical term holds with probability 1-delta, mixing expectation and high-probability.
